Valhalla can return one primary route and up to three alternatives for the baseline. Gate pair requests use through points and return one route each.

Valhalla road preferences

Set these before preparing the route search. They apply to the baseline and every Escape Gate combination. Avoid means Valhalla tries another road when possible; it may still use that road to complete a route.

Unpaved start or end access can still be used. Choose HOV lanes only when your vehicle meets the posted occupancy rules. This search does not use live traffic.

Required: Shotgun Escape Gates

Every new Valhalla search requires reviewed Start Escape Gates and Destination Approach Gates. Each selected gate is a through point with a 200 meter road-search radius; it does not guarantee a road within that radius. Once both gate sets are ready, the exact batch is prepared automatically for your review. The search includes every Start × Destination combination, including no gate at either end. With 16 gates on each side, that is 17 × 17 = 289 Valhalla requests. GO covers each requested ring with overlapping small circles, merges the road data, and removes duplicates. Completed circles are saved; a failed circle requires an explicit Retry. Preparing gates makes no Valhalla or AVM request.

Choose an inner radius up to 19 miles and an outer radius up to 20 miles. The outer radius must be greater than the inner radius. These distances apply to both Start and Destination gates. Adjust any settings, then select GO. Editing settings does not start a search.

24 small circles per trip end — up to 48 Census requests for both ends. Saved circles reduce that number. Nothing starts until GO.

Loading the built-in Chicago starter catalog. After GO, saved circles are reused and missing circles are fetched from Census. No Valhalla or RentCast call is made.

Coordinates for an uncached area are sent to the U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb service. Successful road data enters the shared cache for reuse. Each circle is about 1 mile in radius, with a 25-second and 5 MiB limit. At most 1,024 circles per trip end, 3 at a time. Failed searches stop; Retry resumes saved progress, with at most 3 attempts per circle.

SHOTGUN SCREEN REQUIREDScreen and rank the whole candidate pool first

Every candidate enters the same bounded evidence process before individual route inspection.

1 Screen and compare every route

The whole-pool shotgun screen is required before route inspection or choice. Choose how many unknown, eligible route cells to sample for each enabled route. Known eligible AVM cells are the initial anchors. If any are known, the next unknown cell is farthest from the nearest anchor; with no known values, a one-cell quota targets the unknown midpoint and larger quotas start with the earliest and latest unknowns before spreading. The same rule applies to the initial screen and every additional round. Use each ranking card to include or exclude that route from future evidence rounds; excluded routes stay in the ranking. Shared cells count once and update every route containing them. The ranking is advisory. Every missing or failed lookup stays unknown; failed attempts count against the route quota. Requests run within a bounded plan with no retries, and you still inspect the routes and choose. Each plan shows its exact cells and paid-call ceiling before it starts. Red means below $250 PPSQFT, a geographic value signal rather than a safety measure.

Set the Red Cell level for Route Ranking

Apply a value to rank the candidate routes. Try different values to see how the ranking changes. Each change immediately reclassifies saved evidence, recolors the map cells, and recomputes Red distances and percentages without making a provider call.

Choose and apply the Red Cell level before the first Route Ranking.

Choose Manual or Automatic below to unlock this count. 0 means no new lookups. A positive count selects up to this many unknown, eligible route cells for every enabled route, both initially and in later rounds, prioritizing the positions farthest from known and already selected AVM cells. Toggle route eligibility on each ranking card. Shared cells are requested once and update every route containing them; routes with fewer eligible cells receive fewer. The frozen plan auto-approves after a short pause if its quota, route selection, mode, and candidate cells stay unchanged. The exact deduplicated cell list is capped at 100 calls; failures count and no retries occur.

If the final deduplicated plan exceeds 100 unique calls, lower the per-route count or disable routes.

Selection is deterministic: known eligible AVM cells and newly selected cells are anchors. With known values, each next cell is farthest from its nearest anchor. Without known values, one requested cell targets the unknown midpoint; larger quotas seed the eligible unknown endpoints and then spread by distance. Shared selected cells are requested once.

The whole-pool screen prepares automatically after you set the Red level. Round 0 excludes the bottom third of routes from the current ranking and keeps every route with under 20% known coverage, even when that exceeds the quota. Each later cull fills the smaller quota from the full ranking. A count of 0 checks saved evidence and cache only.

    Automatic route ranking evolution
    With a positive per-route count, selecting Automatic prepares an exact cell list and maximum paid-call ceiling, then starts one cycle of up to 3 additional AVM rounds after a short pause. Round 0 excludes the bottom third of the original routes and keeps every route below 20% known coverage. After each evidence reranking, the bottom third of the previous nominal quota is excluded again. For 27 routes, the nominal INCLUDED counts are 18, then 12, then 8. The best routes in the full current ranking fill those slots, including routes previously EXCLUDED when new AVM evidence improves their rank. Use Stop, select Manual, or change route eligibility to prevent the next group. Up to six requests already sent will finish. After this cycle ends, changing the cell count does not start another. Select Start one Automatic cycle (up to 3 rounds) when you want more evidence.

    3 Inspect a ranked route
    Inspect red cells with Street View before choosing your route.
    

    How scores and coverage work
    Known cell values are weighted by route distance. Valhalla highway classification is not verified in this offshoot, so no highway cells are excluded. Missing values reduce coverage and remain unknown. Red means below your $250 per-square-foot cutoff; it is a geographic value signal, not a measured safety rating.
    The Chicago grid uses 1 km center spacing and fixed cell-center AVM queries. Street View inspection uses a point on your route. Standard subject: single-family home, 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, 1,500 sq ft.
    Saved Route 5 exposure-time aggregates are historical and are not recalculated. Fresh route evaluations show distance and coverage using your cutoff.
